children: Intel Corp. (INTC, Financials), the U.S. chipmaker looking to restore its manufacturing business, may have found an unlikely partner for its large Ohio project.

Reuters said SK Hynix is in talks with Intel on a deal that may allow the South Korean firm to produce memory chips in the U.S. for the first time. One of these options is of particular relevance for Intel.
SK Hynix might lease a portion of Intel's long-delayed Ohio chip plant. Another way is to set up a venture with Intel and the major cloud businesses that are wanting to ensure their memory supply.
That's a positive move for both firms.
SK Hynix is a major provider of high-bandwidth memory used in AI accelerators, and memory demand remains tight as data-center investment continues.

Meanwhile, Intel has had its own problems with the cost and timing of its manufacturing expansion. Two Ohio projects that were initially slated to begin production years ago have been moved to 2030 and 2031. There remains a big hurdle.
South Korea sees modern memory technology as sensitive, thus some production arrangements may require government review. SK Hynix also indicated nothing was settled.

The talks present another option to Ohio investors in Intel: instead of waiting for Intel's manufacturing to materialize totally, part of that expensive footprint could one day be something another major chipmaker might be prepared to pay to utilize.

title: Intel and SK Hynix explore landmark U.S. memory-chip deal
